decision.explanation: The inverse derivative satisfies (f^{-1})'(1)=1/f'(0). Since f'(x)=3x^2+e^x, f'(0)=1, so the requested slope is 1.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Consider the function $f(x)={x}^{3}+{e}^{x}$ and the point $P(0,1)$ that lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is invertible in the vicinity of $P,$ determine the slope of $y={f}^{-1}(x)$ at the point $(1,0).$
after.worked_solution:
We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(0,1).$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={x}^{3}+{e}^{x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =3{x}^{2}+{e}^{x} \\ {f}^{′}(0) & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(0,1)$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(1,0)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(1))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(0)} \\  & =\frac{1}{1} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Consider the function $f(x)={2}^{x}+1.$ Given that $y=f(x)$ is invertible throughout its domain, determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(5).$
after.worked_solution:
To determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(5),$ we use the following formula:

$$
{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(5)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(5))}
$$

First, we calculate the value of ${f}^{-1}(5).$ To do this, we solve the equation ${f}^{-1}(5)=x.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-1}(5) & =x \\ f(x) & =5 \\ {2}^{x}+1 & =5 \\ {2}^{x} & =4 \\ {2}^{x} & ={2}^{2} \\ x & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{-1}(5)=2.$

Now, we calculate ${f}^{′}(2),$ as follows:

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
